problem: ObjectNav methods either map pixels straight to actions or build semantic maps only of areas the agent has already seen. The few spatial-prediction methods anticipate only occupancy or room layout, and none use the uncertainty of their predictions to choose goals. Prior map predictors are also trained on passively collected data, and learned goal policies are target-specific: the reward depends on the target, so a new target needs retraining.
motivation: Humans and animals find objects in unfamiliar homes by using semantic spatial priors (e.g., a fridge is likely near an oven, a sofa is in another room). They also know how far to trust those priors versus exploring further. The paper argues that an agent should hallucinate semantics in unobserved regions and quantify its epistemic uncertainty about them. That uncertainty can then serve two purposes: choosing informative training data, and balancing exploration against exploitation when selecting goals.
key_idea: Train an ensemble of two-stage (occupancy → semantics) top-down map predictors that hallucinate semantics beyond the field of view, fine-tuned on data actively collected by maximizing ensemble disagreement. At test time, select long-term goals by the upper confidence bound (mean + α·std across the ensemble) of the target-class probability, which makes the policy target-independent.
insight:
The ensemble variance of hallucinated semantic maps is a useful signal both for active data collection and for goal selection.
- **Active training:** fine-tuning on variance-selected data beats Offline, Entropy and BALD fine-tuning. Map IoU is 25.6 vs 21.2 for the next best (BALD), and ObjectNav SR is 34.3 vs 30.4, with gains concentrated on hard classes (cushion, counter) and hard episodes.
- **Goal selection:** using uncertainty beats ignoring it. UpperBound reaches SR 34.3 / SPL 13.3, vs 29.8 / 9.3 for Mean, 30.4 / 9.6 for LowerBound and 30.8 / 10.4 for Mixed. Frontier exploration on the same map predictor (FBE) gets only 20.6 SR, so the gain comes from goal selection rather than the map alone.
- **Main bottleneck:** error analysis on 795 hard episodes points to the stop decision rather than goal choice. Oracle stop raises SR from 32.7 to 50.8 and SPL from 12.5 to 33.1; adding GT paths as well reaches 80.5 SR. The selected goals are therefore good, but recognizing arrival and local control fail.
method: Egocentric map inputs: depth is back-projected to a point cloud and ground-projected into a 64×64 egocentric occupancy crop (unknown/occupied/free, 10 cm cells). A separately trained UNet segments the RGB image, and its labels are ground-projected into a semantic crop (27 MP3D-derived classes).

Two-stage semantic map predictor: UNet f_o (ResNet18 encoder) completes occupancy in unobserved areas. Its output is concatenated with the projected semantics and fed to UNet f_s, which predicts per-cell class distributions including unseen regions. Both are trained end-to-end with pixel-wise cross-entropy against GT top-down maps built from MP3D semantic point clouds.

Ensemble epistemic uncertainty: N=4 two-stage models with different random initializations. The mean output approximates P(m|p,ŝ), and the variance across models approximates epistemic uncertainty (query-by-committee / disagreement).

Active training: pre-train on ~900K samples gathered along shortest paths between random locations. Then drive the agent toward global-map locations with maximal class-averaged ensemble variance (Eq. 1, a proxy for information gain), collect ~500K samples, and fine-tune. Entropy and BALD objectives are compared as alternatives.
Global map fusion: local egocentric predictions are registered into a 384×384 global map with Bayesian updates starting from a uniform prior. Uncertainty is accumulated over time.

UCB goal selection: every 20 steps (or when the goal is reached), pick the cell maximizing μ_c + α1·σ_c for target class c (α1=0.1). LowerBound, Mixed (switch at α2=0.75) and Mean variants are ablations. The agent stops when a cell on its path has target probability >0.75 and lies within 0.5 m.
Local policy: an off-the-shelf pretrained DD-PPO PointNav agent (depth + relative goal), not re-trained, outputs low-level actions toward the selected goal.

setting.backbone: Ensemble of 4 two-stage UNet (ResNet18 encoder) semantic map predictors + UNet RGB segmenter (trained from scratch); frozen pretrained DD-PPO PointNav local policy; goal selection is a hand-designed UCB rule (no learned goal policy)
setting.training_data: MP3D train scenes (56) in Habitat: ~900K offline map-prediction samples collected along shortest paths between random locations, plus ~500K actively collected samples (ensemble-variance objective) for fine-tuning. GT top-down semantic/occupancy labels come from MP3D semantic point clouds. The DD-PPO local policy is used as released.
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D (256×256) + noise-free GT pose from the simulator
setting.action_space: high level: goal cell on top-down map; low level: MOVE_FORWARD 0.25 m / TURN_LEFT / TURN_RIGHT 10° / STOP
setting.privileged: noise-free GT agent pose at test time; oracle stop and GT shortest paths are used only in the error-analysis ablations and in the Segm+ANS baseline

numbers_note:
The paper names the distance metric DTS but defines it as 'geodesic distance of agent to the goal at the end of the episode'; it is stored here as DTG. All values are means (the paper also prints ± std errors).
- Evaluation uses self-generated episodes on the MP3D val scenes, not the official Habitat ObjectNav val episodes (21 categories), so numbers are not directly comparable to leaderboard results.
- Privileged oracle variants in Table 4 are omitted: +OracleStop gives SR 50.8 / SPL 33.1, and +GtPath+OracleStop gives SR 80.5 / SPL 52.3.
- Map-prediction quality results are omitted as non-navigation metrics: L2M-Active semantic IoU 25.6 / F1 38.3 / Acc 33.5, and occupancy IoU 48.8 (Tables 2 and 5).
- Per-class and easy-vs-hard results appear only in Figures 4–7.
results: On 2480 self-generated MP3D val ObjectNav episodes (11 categories), L2M-Active-UpperBound reaches SR 34.3 / SPL 13.3. That beats Frontier-based exploration on the same map predictor (SR 20.6) and Segm+ANS with an oracle stop (SR 15.5). On SemExp's 6 categories it gets SR 34.8 vs 28.1 for SemExp, re-run on the same episodes, but a lower SPL (14.8 vs 16.5), because UCB favors exploration. Active variance-based fine-tuning improves semantic map IoU to 25.6, vs 21.2 for BALD and 20.1 for offline training. The main remaining failure is the stop decision: oracle stop lifts SR from 32.7 to 50.8 on hard episodes.
limitations: Ground-projection to a 2D map loses 3D context (e.g., cushions on sofas), which hurts small or stacked categories. Training requires GT semantic point-cloud labels, and the model is biased toward North American/European home layouts.
Assumes noise-free GT pose. The stop heuristic (0.75 probability threshold, 0.5 m) and the frozen DD-PPO local policy are major failure sources, and SPL is low because UCB over-explores.
Evaluated only on self-generated MP3D val episodes with 11 (or 6) categories, not on the official Habitat challenge split, so comparison with other ObjectNav results is limited.
